title: The coefficient prime is a unit in geometric finite-field residue fields
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a prime $\ell\ne p$. If $Y$ is any scheme over $\operatorname{Spec} k$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], then $\ell$ is a unit in $\kappa(y)$ for every $y\in Y$. No finite-type or nonemptiness assumption on $Y$ is needed.

source.place: Finite-field coefficient convention; elementary characteristic calculation underlying Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: The identity #k0=p^a gives characteristic p by charP_of_card_eq_prime_pow. A prime l distinct from p is nonzero by CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime, hence a unit in k0. Map this unit along k0→k, the global-section ring map of the structure morphism Y→Spec k, and residue-field evaluation. Ring maps preserve units and natural-number casts.

proof_origin.place: Elementary argument in the finite-field setting, using the named Mathlib characteristic and ring-map lemmas.
